prompt: Name a planet in the solar system.
note: Authority: IAU 2006 General Assembly Resolution B5, which defines 'planet' and reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet the same year — still the current definition. Eight planets is a closed set under it: unlike the old 'name a moon of Saturn' round this replaced (274 confirmed moons and rising, so any fixed answer list was wrong by construction — a tester hit it with Telesto), no future discovery can add a ninth planet to this list without the IAU redefining the term again. Safe to treat as fixed and complete.

answers.name: Earth
answers.fact: The only planet not named for a Greek or Roman god — the name comes from Old English and Germanic words that just mean 'the ground.'

answers.name: Mars
answers.fact: Home to Olympus Mons: roughly three times Everest's height, and wide enough to blanket the state of Arizona.

answers.name: Jupiter
answers.fact: So massive the solar system's centre of mass sits just outside the Sun's own surface, not at its core.

answers.name: Saturn
answers.fact: Its rings are almost entirely ice — some chunks the size of a grain of sand, others the size of a house.

answers.name: Venus
answers.fact: Rotates backwards, and so slowly that a single day there outlasts its entire year.

answers.name: Mercury
answers.fact: Closest to the Sun, but not the hottest planet — Venus's thick atmosphere traps far more heat.

answers.name: Uranus
answers.fact: Tipped so far onto its side that it essentially rolls around the Sun, likely from an ancient collision.

answers.name: Neptune
answers.fact: Found by mathematics before anyone saw it — its position was predicted from wobbles in Uranus's orbit.

distractors.name: Pluto
distractors.note: Pluto was a planet until 2006, when the IAU reclassified it as a dwarf planet — New Mexico's state legislature has resolved that it's still a planet, at least within the state.

distractors.name: Ceres
distractors.note: The largest object in the asteroid belt — briefly considered a planet in the 1800s, now classified as a dwarf planet like Pluto.

distractors.name: Eris
distractors.note: A dwarf planet out past Neptune, discovered in 2005 — the debate over its status is what pushed astronomers to define 'planet' at all.

distractors.name: Makemake
distractors.note: A dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, named for a creator deity in Rapa Nui (Easter Island) mythology.

distractors.name: Haumea
distractors.note: An egg-shaped dwarf planet that spins so fast, a full day there takes under four hours.
